about: Every numbered row of the subject files transport-rs/docs/parity/*.md (the difference, defect and carried-list rows, table rows `| n |`, numbered lists `n. ` and the `* **n ...` bullets of Phase R round 1) plus the unnumbered rows of the first section (Matched, smoke differences, other differences, Go oddities, now in ipc_process.md), each mapped to the runner case ids that cover its wire-visible part (`cases`) or to an explicit reason it cannot be a wire case (`reason_code`, defined in `reason_codes`). kind: case = covered; partial = the wire-visible part is covered, `reason_code` names why the rest is not; none = no case, `reason_code` says why (DEFERRED-WIRE rows are the next runner slice). `file` (a subject file without .md) and `line` (a line of that file) and `text` are the subject file's, so an edit of a row shows up as a stale map in the audit. `section` is the heading the row sat under when the map was made and is kept as a label. The remaining unnumbered 'Matched'/'Evidence' tables of later slices are mapped per section in `section_map`. Round 2 (R2-38, R2-41): every row carries `digest`, a hash of its whole normalised text in the subject file (`contract_runner.py --audit` fails when a row changed; after a reviewed edit run `--rehash-map`); a row coded UNIT, PANIC, API or TASK with a number of 300 or more names the Rust tests that pin it in `tests` (each must exist as a `fn` under src/ or tests/; `--audit` checks) or gives the reason there is none in `no_test`; a `case` row whose cases are `D-*` ids is executed against both binaries by scripts/wire_deferred.py, not by the full run of the runner.
generated_from: transport-rs/docs/parity/*.md (one file per subject; transport-rs/PARITY.md is the index)

reason_codes.API: Rust API shape, ownership or type-level choice; no wire effect. Pinned by the Rust unit tests named in the row.
reason_codes.TASK: goroutine/channel/context versus tokio task/cancellation mechanics; not visible on the wire, described in transport-rs/DESIGN.md 'Task and cancellation design' and pinned by Rust unit tests.
reason_codes.PANIC: panic containment; no request makes either binary panic on purpose, so there is no wire trigger (see panic_policy in the spec); pinned by Rust tests that inject a panic.
reason_codes.UNIT: internal behaviour (determinism, formatting, queue bounds, config corners) that needs the unit or golden-vector layer; a wire case would need a fake that does not exist yet or cannot make it deterministic.
reason_codes.TIMING: timing, pacing or RTP/SIP-timer behaviour: the trace-diff (Phase 2 item 4, deferred to the next slice), not a request/response case.
reason_codes.REAL: needs a real peer the loopback fakes cannot be: a browser (ICE/DTLS/SRTP), real TLS, real station source-IP rules, the host's interface list. Listed in PARITY 'Not verified' / INTEROP.md.
reason_codes.ENV: depends on the host's resolver, /etc/services or kernel defaults; not deterministic on a test host.
reason_codes.GODEFECT: a defect of the Go code kept or fixed in Rust; recorded for DEV-770, not a conformance expectation (the runner pins Go's wire behaviour, not its bugs).
reason_codes.NOWIRE: not observable through the IPC or the process boundary (logging stream split, unreachable code path).
reason_codes.DEFERRED-WIRE: observable on the wire but no fake behaviour exists for it yet (a case of the retired wire_deferred.py is a `case` row, not this).
reason_codes.TESTMETA: describes how a Go test was ported (goroutine counting, grep tests); not a behaviour.
reason_codes.PROCESS: a carried to-do list of the review, not a behaviour.
reason_codes.TRANSCRIPT: covered: the case ids listed run in every full run against both binaries.
